decision.rationale: M381 and M384 are functionally compatible at the active-descriptor boundary: zero-only compaction, strict PWP selection, canonical descriptors, maximal direct-address runs, D8 credit, tile1 tagged prefetch and exactly two replays agree. They are not cycle-closed. M381 charges matcher, DMA, SRAM latency, backend work, two tail cycles and commit analytically; M384 implements only the controller and exposes external interfaces for matcher results, descriptor/PWP SRAM, DMA readiness/completion and compute service. M387/M391 prove only that this isolated controller logic is equivalent and meets an idealized 3 ns prelayout point. A frozen real-trace miter is therefore the highest-priority next step, while 1.0763828768x remains a four-bottleneck-Conv simulator result rather than RTL-measured performance.

m381_frozen_performance_point.scope: 10 PAFT S10 samples x 4 bottleneck Conv inputs x 432 partitions = 17280 phases
m381_frozen_performance_point.scope_boundary: four-bottleneck-Conv module recurrence; not full network

boundary_consistency.cycle_gap: M384 has never consumed the 51.84M frozen real rows

boundary_consistency.m381_term: q32 nearest/lowest-ID matching and 3000 + matcher_rows + 2 cycles per phase

boundary_consistency.cycle_gap: no matcher RTL or frozen row_valid timestamp schedule
equals one cycle only when phase_seal_ready is immediately asserted

boundary_consistency.m381_term: maximal PWP runs, base + center*576, bytes = len*576
boundary_consistency.cycle_gap: run-ready queueing and physical DMA command acceptance are external

boundary_consistency.m381_term: pattern 64 B, tile weight 6144 B, 576 B per used PWP center, 32 B/cycle, 32-cycle command setup

boundary_consistency.cycle_gap: the environment must withhold replay0 until tile0 DMA completion

boundary_consistency.m381_term: descriptor SRAM fixed L8, request II1, D8, zero per-descriptor blocking
boundary_consistency.m384_implementation: D8 credit and in-order request/response implemented; SRAM remains external
boundary_consistency.cycle_gap: no real SRAM macro/port timing and no frozen workload per-cycle trace

boundary_consistency.m381_term: two replays, each exact_work_o4 + SRAM startup latency
boundary_consistency.m384_implementation: exactly two replays and exact bundle payload; O4 compute backend is outside
boundary_consistency.cycle_gap: bundle_ready service must implement fallback popcount*4 or PWP distance*4+8 exactly

boundary_consistency.m381_term: two tail cycles per phase and 96000 common commit cycles per sample
boundary_consistency.cycle_gap: no proof that all RTL state transitions collapse to the two charged tail cycles

synopsys_boundary.what_it_proves: the isolated M384 controller mapped netlist meets an ideal-clock, no-SPEF, zero-macro prelayout point
what_it_does_not_prove: descriptor or PWP SRAM macro timing

findings.title: No frozen real trace has driven the controller RTL
findings.detail: M384 uses four synthetic normal phases with active counts 0/1/2400/3000. It has not consumed the 17,280 real phases, 51.84M source rows, 21.47M descriptors or 25,443 used-center runs underlying 1.0763829x.

findings.title: Matcher and tile0 DMA timing are outside M384 and not handshaken end-to-end
findings.detail: M384 receives already-selected q32 metadata and has no pattern/tile0-weight DMA completion input. The environment can start replay0 before tile0 payload readiness unless the miter explicitly enforces the M381 schedule.

findings.title: SRAM and backend service assumptions have not been reconciled with RTL cycles
findings.detail: The 1.05x margin tolerates only 0.2955918 serialized cycle per replayed descriptor at cmd32/L8. External SRAM ready/response behavior and backend bundle_ready countdown therefore need exact frozen timestamps; a small hidden bubble can erase the contribution.

findings.title: M381 tail/overlap accounting has no controller-state cycle miter
findings.detail: Seal, run emission, replay start/done, WAIT1 and phase-done handshakes may add or overlap cycles differently from M381's one seal plus two tail cycles. These must be measured and reconciled rather than assumed away.

findings.title: M387/M391 feasibility covers only controller logic
findings.detail: The 3 ns result excludes matcher, DMA, SRAM macros and O4 compute, and uses an ideal clock with no SPEF. It cannot convert a cycle-model speedup into physical throughput.

findings.title: The fair baseline remains a simulator oracle rather than matched RTL
findings.detail: 543,784,143 baseline cycles are frozen and independently reproduced, but there is no corresponding baseline RTL. The miter may validate candidate cycles while speedup remains explicitly simulator-relative.

findings.title: No physical-memory or activity-backed conclusion follows
findings.detail: A successful miter would still use behavioral DMA/SRAM and would emit no physical macro, postroute, SAIF/PTPX, energy, full-network or DATE-headline evidence.

proposed_minimal_executable_miter_contra.name: M393_REALTRACE_M384_CONTROLLER_CYCLE_MITER_R1
proposed_minimal_executable_miter_contra.tool: Synopsys VCS for unmodified exact-SHA M384 RTL plus an independently authored event-oracle

inputs.real_trace: exact M248 manifest and all 40 packed/value payloads
inputs.catalog: exact q32 first-32 nested patterns from M338
inputs.reference: M381 result and M382 independent reconstruction, comparison only after independent event generation

independence: The trace generator must not import the M381 analyzer or M384 testbench oracle
Nearest center must be recomputed over q32 with lowest-ID tie breaking
The cycle oracle and VCS scoreboard must be separate source files with separately frozen hashes
All source payloads, generated phase digests and outputs require double seals

external_cycle_model.matcher: emit 3000 source rows per phase with total matcher duration 3000 + count(popcount(original)>=2) + 2; never hide a controller row stall
external_cycle_model.dma: one ordered engine, 32 B/cycle, 32 setup cycles/command; charge 64 B pattern, 6144 B weight per tile and maximal-run PWP bytes; withhold replay0 until tile0 complete
external_cycle_model.tile1_overlap: accept tagged tile1 prefetch atomically with replay0; return done only after exact tile1 command/data duration; replay1 must wait
external_cycle_model.descriptor_sram: one in-order request/response per cycle, fixed latency 8, D8 credit, no unreported ready or response bubble
external_cycle_model.backend: after each accepted bundle, hold bundle_ready low for exact service: fallback=4*popcount(original), PWP=4*distance+8; freeze edge convention
external_cycle_model.commit: charge the frozen 96000 common cycles per sample outside M384 and report separately

mandatory_outputs: per-phase structural ledger and SHA digest
component cycles for pattern, matcher, seal, runs, tile0 DMA, replay0, exposed tile1 DMA, replay1, tails and commit
actual continuous-request streak, credit/FIFO maxima and all ready/valid stall counts
M381-vs-miter cycle delta with every cycle assigned to a named component
reconciled candidate total and speedup versus the unchanged 543784143-cycle simulator baseline

pass_gates.candidate_total_may_differ_from_50519583: allowed only when the exact delta is named and the frozen result is marked superseded rather than overwritten

negative_controls: inject one extra blocking cycle per descriptor and require the speedup gate to fail
inject an early replay0 before tile0 done and require protocol/scoreboard failure
alter one PWP run length/address and require digest/scoreboard failure
return one response out of order and require fail-closed

decision_after_execution.go: Only zero structural/numeric/event mismatch, zero unattributed cycles and reconciled speedup >=1.05 admit a trace-backed four-bottleneck-Conv module-cycle estimate
decision_after_execution.no_go: Any mismatch, unexplained overlap, hidden stall, incomplete extent or speedup <1.05 closes the current performance contribution pending redesign
